title: Check formatter options on serialized cached-exception fallbacks
applies_when: A receiver accepts both rich in-process objects and serialized or cached representations, with formatting options implemented only on the rich-object branch. Python logging records may carry exc_info locally but only exc_text after SocketHandler serialization.
lesson: Check prior reports and maintainer scope before setup: python-json-logger issue #89 already reports this exact cached-exception case, and #90 is its duplicate. Then trace the actual producer's serialization before inventing a receiver fixture. SocketHandler.makePickle caches formatted exception text and clears the unpicklable exc_info tuple in the transmitted dictionary. A receiver that applies exc_info_as_array only inside formatException can therefore return a string for the cached-text route despite passing ordinary exception tests. Exercise makePickle followed by makeLogRecord on self-generated bytes without opening a socket, and assert the resulting JSON value and type. Keep option-off, direct-exception and explicit caller-override controls; compare the same tests against unchanged and modified source across supported encoders. This local check does not answer a maintainer's separate request for a real production use-case.
avoid_when: A transport may deliberately discard or transform fields under a different documented contract; inspect it rather than assuming round-trip identity. Do not normalize caller-supplied overrides indiscriminately or deserialize untrusted pickle bytes. A local makePickle check does not validate network delivery, pickle security, all subclasses, every Python version or performance. The maintainer conditionally welcomes a small maintainable PR from the original reporter, not a competing submission or an accepted fix; the wontfix label alone does not override that comment. Native passes do not establish a new discovery, real deployment demand or human review. No measured Scout discovery, total-cost or PR-conversion improvement is established; the broader evidence-choice strategy remains a hypothesis.

evidence.note: Python 3.14.3 SocketHandler.makePickle formats exception text before replacing transmitted exc_info with None and pickling the record dictionary. makePickle itself need not open a connection.

BaseJsonFormatter.format uses formatException for exc_info but copies cached exc_text directly; only formatException applies exc_info_as_array. Source-level mismatch, not a public native-test report or maintainer verdict.
Official length-prefixed record serialization and makeLogRecord receiver route; the security warning limits tests to locally generated trusted pickle data.

Prior author-owned report covers the same SocketHandler cached exc_text/array mismatch, with reproducer and proposed repair. Issue #90 is marked duplicate; do not count another local reproduction as fresh discovery.

The owner questions real-world relevance but would consider a sufficiently simple maintainable PR from the reporter. This is conditional interest, not acceptance, an absolute ban or production evidence.
